resources.description: The component challenges only part of the target — a sub-claim or its scope — while leaving the remainder standing (argument-mining stance category)

resources.label: Support
resources.description: The component strengthens the acceptability of the component it targets (standard support relation in argumentation theory and argument mining)

resources.label: Undercut
resources.description: The component attacks the inferential link between the target's data and claim rather than the claim itself — Pollock's undercutting defeater from argumentation theory

resources.label: Evidence Category
resources.description: The kind of support presented for a claim — one of the genuine evidence types, or the declared sentinel value rhetorical_device marking persuasive support that is not evidence proper

resources.label: Analogical
resources.description: Reasoning from parallel cases, metaphors, or comparisons that map a familiar concept onto an unfamiliar one — persuasive but hard to verify

resources.label: Anecdotal
resources.description: Personal stories or singular examples used to illustrate a point — personal narratives, illustrative examples, hypotheticals, and problem-agitation sequences

resources.label: Expert
resources.description: Claims backed by recognised expertise — credentialled expert opinion, institutional authority, or grounded professional experience

resources.label: Logical
resources.description: Reasoning from premises to conclusion through deductive, inductive, or causal argument

resources.label: Rhetorical Device
resources.description: Sentinel support type for passages whose persuasive force comes from a rhetorical device rather than evidence proper; the device hierarchy itself lives in the rhetorical_devices taxonomy

resources.label: Statistical
resources.description: Numerical data, metrics, percentages, and research findings — hard statistics, cited studies, and benchmarks; high persuasive strength and easily verified

resources.label: Testimonial
resources.description: Firsthand accounts, endorsements, and customer stories — quotes, case studies, and public recommendations that persuade through social proof

resources.label: Visual
resources.description: Evidence conveyed through visual artefacts — data visualisations, live or recorded demonstrations, and photographic documentation

resources.label: Evidence Strength
resources.description: The reliability and persuasive weight of the evidence

resources.label: Definitive
resources.description: Verifiable, replicable, peer-reviewed or independently auditable evidence — the highest strength tier

resources.label: Moderate
resources.description: Reasonable but dependent on context or interpretation — analogies, historical precedent, and professional experience

resources.label: Strong
resources.description: Well-sourced and credible but not independently verified — industry reports, expert testimony, and case studies with named clients

resources.label: Weak
resources.description: Suggestive but not reliable for critical decisions — anecdotes, hypotheticals, single examples, and unattributed claims; accumulating weak items does not compound into greater strength

resources.label: Narrative Function
resources.description: The role the evidence plays in the story arc of the argument

resources.label: Outcome Illustration
resources.description: The evidence shows realised results and benefits after the solution is adopted — the closing beat of the argument's story arc

resources.label: Problem Framing
resources.description: The evidence defines and substantiates the problem the argument addresses

resources.label: Situation Setting
resources.description: The evidence establishes context and the current state before any problem is introduced — the opening beat of the argument's story arc

resources.label: Solution Proof
resources.description: The evidence demonstrates that the proposed solution works

resources.label: Stakes Amplification
resources.description: The evidence escalates the cost of inaction or the severity of consequences, building urgency before the solution appears

resources.label: Rhetorical Appeal
resources.description: The Aristotelian appeal category that the evidence or device primarily activates

resources.label: Ethos
resources.description: Persuasion through the speaker's authority, expertise, or trustworthiness — the foundational appeal on which logos and pathos arguments depend to be accepted

resources.label: Kairos
resources.description: Persuasion through the argument's relevance to the current moment or urgency — compelling events, deadlines, and market windows that convert intent to action

resources.label: Logos
resources.description: Persuasion through reason, evidence, and logical argument — strongest with analytical audiences and dependent on evidence quality

resources.label: Mixed
resources.description: The evidence or device activates more than one Aristotelian appeal with no single dominant mode (compositional value over the Aristotelian appeal framework)

resources.label: Pathos
resources.description: Persuasion through emotional connection, values, and empathy — strongest with executive and values-driven audiences, and requiring balance with logos to hold credibility

resources.label: Source Authority
resources.description: The credibility of the evidence source

resources.label: Industry Expert
resources.description: A source deriving credibility from a recognised individual's domain expertise and professional credentials

resources.label: Institutional
resources.description: A source deriving credibility from the position of a recognised institution or standards body rather than an individual (e.g. WHO recommendations, ISO requirements)

resources.label: Peer Reviewed
resources.description: A source vetted through formal scholarly peer review — the most independently verifiable authority tier

resources.label: Practitioner
resources.description: A source grounded in first-hand professional experience rather than formal research or institutional position

resources.label: Unattributed
resources.description: A source with no traceable attribution — the lowest credibility tier, which downgrades the strength of any claim it supports

resources.label: Toulmin Component
resources.description: The role the element plays in an argument structure

resources.label: Backing
resources.description: Support for the warrant itself — the grounds for trusting the reasoning principle rather than the claim

resources.label: Claim
resources.description: The central assertion being argued for — what the speaker wants the audience to accept; typically co-located with its supporting data within a three-sentence window

resources.label: Data
resources.description: The evidence or facts supporting the claim (Toulmin's grounds) — the foundation on which the argument rests, which should be independently verifiable

resources.label: Qualifier
resources.description: The degree of certainty or the conditions attached to the claim — how strongly it is asserted (probably, usually, in most cases)

resources.label: Rebuttal
resources.description: Exceptions or counterarguments to the claim — the conditions under which it would not hold

resources.label: Warrant
resources.description: The logical bridge connecting data to claim — the reasoning principle that makes the data relevant; when absent, the audience must infer it, a primary source of argument failure

resources.label: Assess Performance
resources.description: Gagné's eighth event: testing whether learners have met the objectives.

resources.label: Elicit Performance
resources.description: Gagné's sixth event: having learners practise what they have learned.

resources.label: Enhance Retention and Transfer
resources.description: Gagné's ninth event: helping learners retain the learning and apply it in new situations and on the job.

resources.label: Gain Attention
resources.description: Gagné's first event of instruction: capturing the learner's attention and interest so they are ready to receive the lesson.

resources.label: Inform Learners of Objectives
resources.description: Gagné's second event: telling learners what they will be able to do by the end, so they can organise their attention around it.

resources.label: Present the Content
resources.description: Gagné's fourth event: presenting the new material in organised, meaningful chunks.

resources.label: Provide Feedback
resources.description: Gagné's seventh event: giving learners specific, timely information about their performance.

resources.label: Provide Learning Guidance
resources.description: Gagné's fifth event: guiding learners with examples, demonstrations and cues that help them encode the material.

resources.label: Stimulate Recall of Prior Learning
resources.description: Gagné's third event: bringing relevant prior knowledge back to mind so new material can attach to it.

resources.label: Argument
resources.description: A reason supporting or opposing a position.

resources.label: Generalizes
resources.description: Connects an issue to a more specific issue it subsumes.

resources.label: Is-suggested-by
resources.description: Connects an issue to the deliberation node that prompted it.

resources.label: Issue
resources.description: A question or problem requiring deliberation.

resources.label: Objects-to
resources.description: Connects an opposing argument to a position.

resources.label: Position
resources.description: A proposed resolution of an issue.

resources.label: Questions
resources.description: Connects an issue to the deliberation node it challenges.

resources.label: Replaces
resources.description: Connects an issue to the issue it supersedes.

resources.label: Responds-to
resources.description: Connects a proposed position to its issue.

resources.label: Specializes
resources.description: Connects an issue to a broader issue it narrows.

resources.label: Supports
resources.description: Connects a favourable argument to a position.

resources.label: Concept
resources.description: The knowledge kind of a category or class of things grouped by shared attributes, answering what something is; its typical statement is a definition with examples.

resources.label: Fact
resources.description: The knowledge kind of one specific, verifiable datum — a name, a figure, a date or a specification — stated without a sequence in time; unlike a category it names no class, and unlike a rule it does not hold across cases.

resources.label: Principle
resources.description: The knowledge kind of a rule, policy, axiom or cause-and-effect relationship that holds across cases and licenses a prediction or a decision, as a law or a policy does.

resources.label: Procedure
resources.description: The knowledge kind of an ordered set of steps that a person carries out to accomplish a task; the reader is the actor, which separates it from knowledge of how a system runs on its own.

resources.label: Process
resources.description: The knowledge kind of how a system works or how events flow through stages, understood by the reader rather than performed by them; the system or the event sequence is the actor, which separates it from knowledge of steps a person carries out.

resources.label: Advanced Learner
resources.description: A learner with substantial domain knowledge seeking mastery by refining and extending their schemas; comfortable with abstraction, self-directed and tolerant of high cognitive load.

resources.label: Expert Learner
resources.description: A learner with extensive, deep expertise seeking new insight by restructuring their schemas for new paradigms; prefers abstraction, is fully autonomous and tolerates very high cognitive load.

resources.label: Intermediate Learner
resources.description: A learner with foundational knowledge who is building competence by integrating new material with what they know; handles some abstraction, is developing self-direction and tolerates moderate cognitive load.

resources.label: Novice Learner
resources.description: A learner new to the domain with minimal prior knowledge, still building foundational schemas; needs concrete examples before abstraction and external guidance to regulate their learning, and tolerates little cognitive load.

resources.label: Achievement-Oriented
resources.description: A learner motivation driven by goals, recognition and measurable progress — mastery, credentials, performance metrics, demonstrated competency and career advancement.

resources.label: Craft Mastery
resources.description: A learner motivation driven by depth and excellence in the craft itself.

resources.label: Curiosity-Driven
resources.description: A learner motivation driven by understanding, novelty and exploration — new information, the why behind a thing and intellectual challenge.

resources.label: Get the Job Done
resources.description: A learner motivation driven by immediate task completion, for which learning is a means and not an end.

resources.label: Operational Stability
resources.description: A learner motivation driven by keeping systems and processes running safely.

resources.label: Outcome Accountability
resources.description: A learner motivation driven by owning and evidencing a business outcome.

resources.label: Problem Solver
resources.description: A learner motivation driven by resolving concrete, present problems — immediate applicability, real-world problems, practical solutions and efficiency gains.

resources.label: Risk Reduction
resources.description: A learner motivation driven by avoiding failure, exposure or wasted investment.

resources.label: Social Learner
resources.description: A learner motivation driven by peers, community and shared practice — peer interaction, shared learning, discussion and belonging.

resources.label: Change Enablement Audience
resources.description: A learning situation in which people are segmented for communications, impact analysis and operational readiness during a programme or system change, rather than for capability design.

resources.label: Compliance-Driven Learner
resources.description: A learning situation in which the learner is motivated chiefly by an obligation, a deadline or an audit requirement.

resources.label: Just-in-Time Learner
resources.description: A learning situation in which the learner is under immediate pressure or blocked on a live task or incident and seeks the minimum clarity needed to act now.

resources.label: Onboarding-Window Learner
resources.description: A learning situation inside the initial deployment or onboarding period of a product, when motivation and organisational attention are at their peak.

resources.label: Renewal-Pressure Audience
resources.description: A learning situation in which an audience is engaged while evidence of value is assembled ahead of a renewal or expansion decision.

resources.label: Advanced
resources.description: The learning level of content demanding high proficiency — specialisation, complex integration, optimisation, troubleshooting and difficult problem solving.

resources.label: Expert
resources.description: The learning level of content at architecture-level design, scalability, thought leadership and expert or master practice.

resources.label: Foundational
resources.description: The learning level of content covering core concepts, basic workflows, essential terminology and introductory understanding of the subject.

resources.label: Intermediate
resources.description: The learning level of content covering broader feature sets, configuration options, applied use cases and deeper understanding of the subject.

resources.label: bloom_level
resources.description: Bloom's Revised Taxonomy cognitive level from Remember (1) to Create (6)

resources.label: Analyze
resources.description: Level 4 — break material into constituent parts and determine how they relate to structure and purpose; strong verbs include differentiate, diagnose, and deconstruct

resources.label: Apply
resources.description: Level 3 — carry out or use a procedure in a given situation; strong verbs include demonstrate, implement, and solve

resources.label: Create
resources.description: Level 6 — put elements together to form a new, coherent, or functional whole; strong verbs include design, build, and formulate

resources.label: Evaluate
resources.description: Level 5 — make judgements based on criteria and standards; strong verbs include critique, justify, and recommend

resources.label: Remember
resources.description: Level 1 — retrieve, recognise, or recall relevant knowledge from long-term memory; strong verbs include define, list, and identify

resources.label: Understand
resources.description: Level 2 — construct meaning by interpreting, classifying, comparing, or explaining in one's own words; strong verbs include explain, summarise, and compare

resources.label: cognitive_category
resources.description: Higher-order vs lower-order thinking classification

resources.label: Higher Order Thinking
resources.description: Analyze, Evaluate, and Create — transfer, judgment, and creation, indicating deep learning

resources.label: Lower Order Thinking
resources.description: Remember, Understand, and Apply — foundation knowledge and skill, necessary but not sufficient for transfer

resources.label: objective_quality
resources.description: ABCD formula compliance and measurability quality rating

resources.label: Acceptable
resources.description: Objective uses a measurable verb but leaves condition or degree implicit — usable, though short of best practice

resources.label: Strong
resources.description: Objective satisfies the full ABCD formula — a measurable Bloom-aligned verb with explicit condition and degree of success

resources.label: Weak Or Invalid
resources.description: Objective rests on an unmeasurable verb such as understand, know, or appreciate, or lacks an observable behaviour, so it cannot be assessed as written

resources.label: emotional_tone
resources.description: Affective register of the narrative segment

resources.label: Celebratory
resources.description: Triumphant, achievement-focused register marking success and validation

resources.label: Concerned
resources.description: Worried, cautionary register highlighting risks — problem-aware

resources.label: Inspirational
resources.description: Motivating, visionary, aspirational register — the 'art of the possible'

resources.label: Neutral
resources.description: Factual, informational, objective, balanced register — typical of agenda and methodology segments

resources.label: Optimistic
resources.description: Positive, hopeful, forward-looking, opportunity-focused register

resources.label: Urgent
resources.description: Time-sensitive, pressing register signalling that immediate action is needed — the 'burning platform'

resources.label: soar_stage
resources.description: SOAR narrative framework stage alignment

resources.label: Action
resources.description: Stage presenting the proposed solution and the specific mechanism for seizing the opportunity — concrete rather than aspirational

resources.label: Opportunity
resources.description: Stage identifying the gap, problem, or chance and setting the stakes — tension and urgency are expected here

resources.label: Result
resources.description: Closing stage showing outcomes, benefits, and value — requires quantified proof to hold credibility

resources.label: Situation
resources.description: Opening stage establishing shared context, background, and current state — not the place for opportunity or CTA content

resources.label: story_function
resources.description: Narrative role of a content segment within the overall story arc

resources.label: Action
resources.description: Explains the specific mechanism by which the solution operates (SOAR Action stage) — describes how, not just what, unlike solution

resources.label: CTA
resources.description: Issues the call to action — next steps, what the audience should do, or contact information

resources.label: Evidence
resources.description: Provides proof — data, testimonials, case studies, or validation

resources.label: Insight
resources.description: Reveals key understanding — an 'aha' moment, discovery, or root cause

resources.label: Opportunity
resources.description: Reframes a problem as a positive opportunity or unrealised value gap (SOAR Opportunity stage) — forward-looking and value-anchored, unlike problem, which describes pain

resources.label: Problem
resources.description: Identifies pain points, challenges, obstacles, conflicts, or market shifts

resources.label: Result
resources.description: Shows outcomes, benefits, transformation, ROI, or future state

resources.label: Setup
resources.description: Establishes context, introduces the situation, sets the scene, or provides the agenda

resources.label: Solution
resources.description: Presents the answer — approach, methodology, product, or capability

resources.label: Tension
resources.description: Builds stakes, urgency, consequences of inaction, or competitive threat

resources.label: Validated Result
resources.description: Shows independently verified, quantified outcomes requiring a named customer, specific metric, and auditable source — stricter than result and the highest evidence quality

resources.label: Audience Impact
resources.description: The strength of the hook's effect on audience engagement

resources.label: High
resources.description: Strong engagement effect — characteristic of question, statistic, bold-claim, and silence hooks

resources.label: Low
resources.description: Minimal engagement effect — the hook barely lifts attention above an unhooked opening

resources.label: Medium
resources.description: Moderate engagement effect — characteristic of quotation hooks, which engage without commanding the room

resources.label: Very High
resources.description: The top impact tier — characteristic of story, demonstration, and entrance hooks that create maximum engagement and memorability

resources.label: Hook Category
resources.description: The primary type of opening hook

resources.label: Bold Claim
resources.description: Opens with a provocative, contrarian, or surprising assertion that contradicts expectations and demands resolution

resources.label: Demonstration
resources.description: Opens with a live demo, visual reveal, or interactive audience moment — concrete experience rather than abstraction

resources.label: Entrance
resources.description: The hook that begins before a single word is spoken — the act of entering the space, walking to the stage, and taking position constitutes the opening communication

resources.label: Question
resources.description: Opens with a question — rhetorical, direct, provocative, or hypothetical — to trigger curiosity and immediate mental engagement

resources.label: Quotation
resources.description: Opens with a relevant quote from an authority figure, inheriting the credibility of its source

resources.label: Silence
resources.description: Opens with deliberate silence or an extended pause to create tension and heightened attention before the first words

resources.label: Statistic
resources.description: Opens with a surprising number or data point to establish credibility and urgency

resources.label: Story
resources.description: Opens with a narrative — personal, customer, historical, or hypothetical — that creates emotional connection and context

resources.label: Narrative Function
resources.description: The role the hook plays in the presentation's narrative arc

resources.label: Attention Capture
resources.description: The hook seizes audience focus in the opening moments, before any content lands

resources.label: Context Setting
resources.description: The hook establishes the situation and shared ground the presentation builds on

resources.label: Credibility Building
resources.description: The hook establishes the speaker's authority and trustworthiness at the outset — the function of statistic and quotation openings

resources.label: Emotional Priming
resources.description: The hook puts the audience in the affective state the narrative requires before the argument begins

resources.label: Presence Establishment
resources.description: The hook establishes the speaker's physical command of the room before or without words — the function of entrance and silence openings

resources.label: Problem Framing
resources.description: The hook surfaces the problem the presentation will address

resources.label: Presentation Context
resources.description: The setting in which the presentation is delivered

resources.label: Executive Briefing
resources.description: Time-constrained senior audience that values directness and data — favours statistic, bold-claim, and quotation hooks over exercises and extended stories

resources.label: Keynote
resources.description: Large-audience conference setting needing emotional impact and memorability — favours entrance, story, bold-claim, demonstration, and silence hooks, since the first impression is set before a word is spoken

resources.label: Sales Presentation
resources.description: Context in which relevance and urgency must be established quickly — favours story, statistic, and question hooks

resources.label: Training Session
resources.description: Learning context that benefits from engagement and relatability — favours question, demonstration, and story hooks

resources.label: Webinar
resources.description: Remote setting where immediate engagement is needed to prevent multitasking — favours question, statistic, and story hooks; silence and demonstration translate poorly

resources.label: Psychological Mechanism
resources.description: The cognitive principle that makes the hook effective

resources.label: Authority Bias
resources.description: Attributed statements inherit the credibility of their source — the mechanism behind quotation hooks

resources.label: Cognitive Dissonance
resources.description: A claim that contradicts expectations creates discomfort the audience is driven to resolve — the mechanism behind bold-claim hooks

resources.label: Curiosity Gap
resources.description: Unresolved questions trigger dopamine-driven attention until the open loop is closed (Loewenstein 1994) — the mechanism behind question hooks

resources.label: Expectancy Violation
resources.description: Behaviour that breaks contextual norms — such as silence in a speaking context — sharply heightens attention; the mechanism behind silence hooks

resources.label: Experiential Learning
resources.description: Concrete experience is more memorable than abstraction — the mechanism behind demonstration hooks

resources.label: Halo Effect
resources.description: A single positive first impression cascades into positive judgements of all other speaker attributes (Thorndike 1920; Nisbett & Wilson 1977)

resources.label: Isolation Effect
resources.description: A surprising item standing out from uniform surroundings is disproportionately noticed and remembered (Von Restorff 1933) — the mechanism behind statistic hooks

resources.label: Neural Coupling
resources.description: Stories synchronise speaker and listener brain activity, creating shared engagement — the mechanism behind story hooks

resources.label: Thin Slicing
resources.description: Audiences form strong, durable impressions from milliseconds of expressive behaviour (Ambady & Rosenthal 1992) — the mechanism behind entrance and stillness hooks

resources.label: AltLex
resources.description: Alternative lexical expression.

resources.label: AltLexC
resources.description: Lexicosyntactic connective construction.

resources.label: EntRel
resources.description: Entity coherence without a discourse sense.

resources.label: Explicit
resources.description: Overt discourse connective.

resources.label: Hypophora
resources.description: Question followed by its answer.

resources.label: Implicit
resources.description: Inferred discourse connective.

resources.label: NoRel
resources.description: No annotated discourse or entity relation.

resources.label: audience_experience_level
resources.description: Learner experience level the framework is optimised for

resources.label: Experienced
resources.description: Learners with substantial domain expertise, best served by self-directed, discovery, and peer-based approaches

resources.label: Intermediate
resources.description: Learners with working foundational knowledge, ready for problem-centred practice and social learning with reduced scaffolding

resources.label: Novice
resources.description: Learners with little or no prior domain knowledge, needing directive instruction, structured sequencing, and full scaffolding

resources.label: bloom_level_alignment
resources.description: Bloom's taxonomy level the framework is best suited to develop

resources.label: Analyze
resources.description: Framework is best suited to developing decomposition of material and diagnosis of how parts relate, as in problem-based learning

resources.label: Apply
resources.description: Framework is best suited to developing execution of procedures and skills in context, as in mastery learning or social modelling

resources.label: Create
resources.description: Framework is best suited to developing design and production of novel work, as in discovery learning or action learning

resources.label: Evaluate
resources.description: Framework is best suited to developing criterion-based judgement and critique, as in Kolb's cycle or communities of practice

resources.label: Remember
resources.description: Framework is best suited to developing retrieval and recognition of facts and terminology, as in spaced repetition

resources.label: Understand
resources.description: Framework is best suited to developing interpretation and explanation of concepts in the learner's own words

resources.label: delivery_format
resources.description: Delivery modality for which the framework is most effective

resources.label: Blended
resources.description: Delivery combining live facilitated sessions with self-paced components in one structured journey

resources.label: eLearning
resources.description: Self-paced interactive digital delivery completed without a live facilitator

resources.label: ILT
resources.description: Instructor-led training delivered live and in person to a cohort

resources.label: On The Job
resources.description: Delivery embedded in real work, where learning happens while performing actual tasks, supported by coaching or performance support

resources.label: Self Directed
resources.description: Learner-controlled delivery in which the individual chooses what, when, and how to study, without an imposed pathway

resources.label: Virtual ILT
resources.description: Instructor-led training delivered live over video conferencing rather than in a physical room

resources.label: learning_paradigm
resources.description: Foundational theoretical orientation of the pedagogical framework

resources.label: Behaviourist
resources.description: Learning is a change in observable behaviour produced by stimulus-response relationships and reinforcement (Skinner, Pavlov, Watson)

resources.label: Cognitivist
resources.description: Learning is internal information processing — attention, encoding, schema formation, and retrieval (Piaget, Ausubel, Bruner)

resources.label: Constructivist
resources.description: Learners actively construct knowledge through experience, reflection, and interaction with their environment (Piaget, Dewey, Vygotsky)

resources.label: Experiential
resources.description: Learning is a cyclical process of concrete experience, reflective observation, conceptual abstraction, and active experimentation (Dewey, Kolb, Schön)

resources.label: Humanist Andragogical
resources.description: Adult learners are self-directed, experience-rich, and motivated by relevance to their personal and professional goals (Knowles, Maslow, Rogers)

resources.label: Social Learning
resources.description: Learning occurs through observation of others, social interaction, and participation in communities of practice (Vygotsky, Bandura, Lave and Wenger)

resources.label: narrative_shape
resources.description: Vonnegut story shape archetype governing emotional arc

resources.label: Cinderella
resources.description: Rises, suffers a setback, then achieves ultimate triumph — the Vonnegut shape of resilience and turnaround narratives

resources.label: Icarus
resources.description: Rises to a height, then falls from grace — the Vonnegut shape of cautionary tales and risk presentations

resources.label: Man In Hole
resources.description: Starts okay, falls into trouble, climbs out successfully — the Vonnegut shape of problem-solving presentations ('we faced a crisis, here is how we solved it')

resources.label: Rags To Riches
resources.description: Starts low and rises steadily to success — the Vonnegut shape of growth stories and transformation narratives

resources.label: slide_density
resources.description: Information density category governing dwell time and design approach

resources.label: Dense
resources.description: Multiple data points or complex visuals with an extended dwell time — analysis and detailed-evidence slides requiring careful organisation

resources.label: Lean
resources.description: One concept and minimal text with the shortest dwell time — statement slides, transitions, and emotional beats built for maximum impact

resources.label: Moderate
resources.description: Two to three balanced points with a short dwell time — standard information delivery with clear hierarchy

resources.label: Slidument
resources.description: A document disguised as a slide, demanding document-length dwell time — to be avoided in live presentations and acceptable only as leave-behind reference material

resources.label: structural_framework
resources.description: Overarching presentation narrative framework applied to the whole deck

resources.label: Duarte Sparkline
resources.description: Nancy Duarte's structure alternating 'what is' and 'what could be' to build tension and longing, climaxing in the 'new bliss' of the transformed future

resources.label: Minto Pyramid
resources.description: Barbara Minto's answer-first structure — a single governing thought at the top, supported by MECE key-line arguments and evidence beneath (BLUF principle)

resources.label: Monroe Sequence
resources.description: Alan Monroe's five-stage persuasive structure — Attention, Need, Satisfaction, Visualization, Action — mirroring the psychological journey from indifference to commitment

resources.label: Soar Framework
resources.description: Four-beat Situation-Opportunity-Action-Result narrative structure for business presentations, with a matching visual and emotional arc per beat

resources.label: Vonnegut Shape
resources.description: Framework applying Kurt Vonnegut's story-shape archetypes — man in hole, rags to riches, Icarus, Cinderella — to govern the deck's emotional arc

resources.label: title_strategy
resources.description: Headline type applied to communicate the slide's key assertion

resources.label: Action Title
resources.description: A title that makes an assertion or claim (subject-verb-outcome), conveying the slide's takeaway immediately and supporting skimmability

resources.label: Label Title
resources.description: A title that merely names the topic, leaving the audience to extract the point from the slide body — acceptable only for reference slides, exploratory workshops, and section dividers

resources.label: Question Title
resources.description: A title that poses a question the slide then answers, creating engagement and curiosity at the cost of directness

resources.label: Instructional Form
resources.description: An artefact form that teaches — it carries a full alignment chain from objective through activity to evidence, and discharges a taught disposition

resources.label: Deck
resources.description: A presentation deck carrying a taught narrative

resources.label: Formal Module
resources.description: A formal course module delivered as structured instruction

resources.label: Podcast Episode
resources.description: A scripted audio episode, including reinforcement and discussion episodes

resources.label: Video
resources.description: A scripted spoken video such as an explainer or narrated training piece

resources.label: Workshop Session
resources.description: A facilitated live session, in-room or virtual

resources.label: Support Form
resources.description: An artefact form that supports performance at the moment of need rather than teaching; it discharges a performance-support disposition

resources.label: Aide-Memoire
resources.description: A compact memory prompt that cues recall of already-learned material

resources.label: Job Aid
resources.description: A task-anchored reference used during work, reachable at the moment of apply

resources.label: Performance Support
resources.description: In-workflow support embedded at the point of work

resources.label: aristotelian_appeal
resources.description: Primary appeal mode of the device where applicable — logos, ethos, pathos, or the opportune-moment appeal kairos

resources.label: Ethos
resources.description: Appeal to credibility — persuasion through demonstrated expertise, character, or trustworthiness

resources.label: Kairos
resources.description: Appeal to the opportune moment — timing the message so its claim lands when the audience is most receptive; the post-Aristotelian fourth appeal alongside logos, ethos, and pathos

resources.label: Logos
resources.description: Appeal to reason — persuasion through evidence and logical argument

resources.label: Pathos
resources.description: Appeal to emotion — persuasion through emotional resonance, storytelling, or connection to values

resources.label: device_family
resources.description: Rhetorical device family grouping by functional mechanism

resources.label: Amplification
resources.description: Devices that heighten intensity, urgency, or emotional weight — hyperbole, climax, and litotes

resources.label: Aristotelian Appeals
resources.description: The family establishing the rational, emotional, and credibility bases of persuasion — logos, ethos, and pathos operating together rather than as figures of speech

resources.label: Balance
resources.description: Devices that create clarity and impact through parallel or opposing structures — antithesis, chiasmus, isocolon, and parallelism

resources.label: Comparison
resources.description: Devices that make the abstract concrete through comparison, contrast, or illustration — metaphor, simile, extended analogy, and antimetabole

resources.label: Engagement
resources.description: Devices that create audience participation, identification, or curiosity — rhetorical question, inclusive we, apostrophe, and procatalepsis

resources.label: Repetition
resources.description: Devices that create rhythm, emphasis, and memorability through structural repetition — anaphora, epistrophe, symploce, tricolon, and anadiplosis

resources.label: Structural
resources.description: Devices that guide the audience through content with clear signalling and organisation — three-part structure, aposiopesis, and conduplicatio — reducing cognitive load

resources.label: power_level
resources.description: Persuasive impact rating of the rhetorical device when applied correctly

resources.label: High
resources.description: Strong impact — the foundation of effective rhetoric

resources.label: Low
resources.description: Subtle impact — often structural rather than rhetorical in effect

resources.label: Medium
resources.description: Useful support — effective in combination with other devices

resources.label: Very High
resources.description: Maximum persuasive impact — reserved for high-stakes moments only

resources.label: structural_framework
resources.description: Meta-level rhetorical framework for overall message architecture

resources.label: Monroe Sequence
resources.description: Alan Monroe's five-stage Attention-Need-Satisfaction-Visualization-Action sequence — especially effective for change management and sales narratives

resources.label: SCQA
resources.description: Situation-Complication-Question-Answer — Barbara Minto's top-down structure that delivers the answer before the supporting evidence, per the BLUF principle

resources.label: analogy
resources.description: Transfers a comparison across otherwise different cases.

resources.label: comment

resources.label: concession

resources.label: conclusion

resources.label: elaboration-set-member

resources.label: Assessment Scope
resources.description: The scope at which evaluation is applied — a content granularity from single interaction to whole portfolio, or a cross-cutting scope such as workplace transfer or delivery modality

resources.label: Deck Level
resources.description: Holistic evaluation of an entire presentation or content asset

resources.label: Interaction Level
resources.description: Evaluation of a single atomic interaction or question — immediate response validation at the card or item level

resources.label: Microlearning Level
resources.description: Evaluation of a short microlearning sequence — embedded quick checks and micro-feedback loops; the span it covers is library knowledge

resources.label: Modality Level
resources.description: Evaluation applied across one delivery modality, comparing content within that channel rather than judging a single content unit

resources.label: Portfolio Level
resources.description: Evaluation aggregated across multiple content assets — consistency, brand alignment, and quality trend

resources.label: Section Level
resources.description: Evaluation of a group of slides or a content section for structure, narrative flow, and evidence quality

resources.label: Slide Level
resources.description: Evaluation of a single slide or content unit for qualities such as visual clarity and cognitive load

resources.label: Workplace Level
resources.description: Evaluation applied to on-the-job performance after learning — workplace transfer rather than a content unit

resources.label: Cognitive Level (Bloom's)
resources.description: The cognitive complexity tier of the learning objective or assessment item, aligned to Bloom's Revised Taxonomy (Anderson & Krathwohl 2001)

resources.label: Analyse
resources.description: Requires breaking material into parts and determining how they relate to structure and purpose

resources.label: Apply
resources.description: Requires carrying out or using a procedure in a given situation

resources.label: Create
resources.description: Requires assembling elements into a new, coherent, or original whole

resources.label: Evaluate
resources.description: Requires making judgements based on criteria and standards

resources.label: Remember
resources.description: Requires retrieval or recognition of knowledge from long-term memory

resources.label: Understand
resources.description: Requires constructing meaning — interpreting, classifying, comparing, or explaining

resources.label: Evaluative Function
resources.description: The purpose and audience of the evaluation

resources.label: Benchmarking
resources.description: Compares quality against standards, peers, or historical performance, yielding comparative scores and percentile positioning

resources.label: Diagnostic
resources.description: Identifies specific strengths, weaknesses, and prerequisite gaps before or at the start of learning, to target improvement

resources.label: Formative
resources.description: Provides in-progress feedback that guides iterative improvement during the creation or learning process

resources.label: Ipsative
resources.description: Evaluates performance against the learner's or creator's own previous results rather than an external standard, tracking personal growth over time

resources.label: Summative
resources.description: Provides a final quality judgement for a completed asset, read by stakeholders, reviewers, and quality assurance

resources.label: Transfer Evaluation
resources.description: Assesses application of learning in the workplace after the formal learning event, at Kirkpatrick L3-L4, at the booster intervals the library states

resources.label: Quality Domain
resources.description: The broad area of quality the dimension belongs to

resources.label: Argument Quality
resources.description: Dimensions covering the strength and credibility of claims and evidence — evidence quality, logical coherence, and source credibility

resources.label: Communication Quality
resources.description: Dimensions covering how effectively content conveys its message — clarity, structure, engagement, and personalisation of tone

resources.label: Design Quality
resources.description: Dimensions covering visual presentation, aesthetic effectiveness, and cognitive readability — hierarchy, typography, colour contrast, imagery, and layout

resources.label: Inclusion Quality
resources.description: Dimensions covering accessibility, diversity, universal design, and cultural appropriateness for diverse audiences

resources.label: Learning Quality
resources.description: Dimensions covering cognitive load management, instructional effectiveness, multimedia principles, and transfer to real-world application

resources.label: Validity Integrity Quality
resources.description: Dimensions covering whether instruments measure what they claim to measure and whether scores are free from systematic bias or construct-irrelevant variance

resources.label: Rubric Type
resources.description: The structural approach used for scoring

resources.label: Analytic
resources.description: Scores each dimension separately with distinct criteria per level — detailed diagnostic feedback at the cost of time to apply

resources.label: Confidence Weighted
resources.description: Adjusts each response's score by the learner's expressed confidence — rewarding calibrated certainty and penalising overconfident guessing to incentivise epistemic accuracy

resources.label: Holistic
resources.description: Assigns a single overall score from a general impression across all dimensions — fast to apply but low in diagnostic value

resources.label: Single Point
resources.description: Defines only the proficient level, with feedback noting deviations above or below — encourages qualitative feedback but needs skilled assessors

resources.label: Weighted
resources.description: Analytic rubric with different importance weights per dimension, reflecting strategic priorities in the composite score

resources.label: Score Tier
resources.description: The performance level assigned to evaluated content

resources.label: Developing
resources.description: Approaching expectations — shows promise but needs refinement; its score band is library knowledge

resources.label: Exemplary
resources.description: Exceeds expectations and models best practice; its score band is library knowledge

resources.label: Needs Improvement
resources.description: Below expectations — fundamental issues to address; its score band is library knowledge

resources.label: Proficient
resources.description: Meets expectations — solid and effective; its score band is library knowledge

resources.label: Alternation
resources.description: Presents disjunctive alternatives without asserting either constituent.

resources.label: Attribution
resources.description: Relates an agent to attributed content without committing to the content's truth.

resources.label: Background
resources.description: Supplies contextual information about an event or object; event-state background overlaps temporally.

resources.label: Complex Discourse Unit
resources.description: A group of discourse constituents interpreted together as a discourse unit.

resources.label: Commentary
resources.description: Adds an evaluation or opinion about the first constituent.

resources.label: Consequence
resources.description: Relates conditional antecedent to consequent without asserting either constituent.

resources.label: Continuation
resources.description: Adds a contribution at the same discourse level under a shared topic.

resources.label: Contrast
resources.description: Juxtaposes comparable constituents through opposition or denial of an expected consequence.

resources.label: Coordinating Relation
resources.description: Connects constituents at the same level of discourse structure.

resources.label: Elementary Discourse Unit
resources.description: An elementary segment contributing a discourse representation.

resources.label: Elaboration
resources.description: Develops a constituent through more specific information about its content.

resources.label: Explanation
resources.description: Provides an explanatory cause for the preceding constituent's situation.

resources.label: Narration
resources.description: Relates successive events belonging to a coherent narrative sequence.

resources.label: Parallel
resources.description: Relates constituents through corresponding semantic structure.

resources.label: Precondition
resources.description: Presents an event preceding the first constituent; this is reverse narration, not a logical conditional.

resources.label: Result
resources.description: Presents a consequence of the preceding constituent's situation.

resources.label: Right Frontier Constraint
resources.description: Restricts incremental attachment to the latest constituent and its available structural superordinates.

resources.label: Source
resources.description: Relates communicated content to its source; both constituents are treated as veridical.

resources.label: Subordinating Relation
resources.description: Connects a constituent to one elaborating or explaining it at a subordinate level.

resources.label: Certainty Direction
resources.description: Whether the marker increases, decreases, or does not affect perceived certainty

resources.label: Decreases
resources.description: The marker lowers the perceived certainty of the proposition — the direction of hedge markers

resources.label: Increases
resources.description: The marker raises the perceived certainty of the proposition — the direction of boost markers

resources.label: Neutral
resources.description: The marker leaves perceived certainty unchanged, expressing attitude rather than confidence — the direction of position markers

resources.label: Discourse Role
resources.description: The function the stance marker performs within the discourse structure

resources.label: Attribution
resources.description: Identifies the source or basis of a claim for credibility and transparency (according to, as X states, studies show)

resources.label: Boosting
resources.description: Strengthens the speaker's commitment and persuasive force — assertiveness and confidence projection in pitches, leadership, and advocacy

resources.label: Discounting
resources.description: Acknowledges a counterpoint or concession before reasserting the main claim with greater force — the concession-then-assertion pattern that pre-empts objections while the post-marker assertion carries the speaker's actual stance

resources.label: Evaluation
resources.description: Signals the speaker's judgement about propositions or events — opinion formation, critique, and commentary

resources.label: Hedging
resources.description: Protects the speaker from full commitment to a proposition — face-saving, academic caution, and diplomatic or risk communication

resources.label: Marker Type
resources.description: The primary category of stance marker

resources.label: Boost
resources.description: A marker that increases the certainty or force of a claim — strong modals, certainty adverbs, emphatics, and universal quantifiers (must, definitely, always)

resources.label: Hedge
resources.description: A marker that reduces the certainty or force of a claim — modal verbs, epistemic adverbs, perception verbs, and approximators (might, possibly, seems to)

resources.label: Position
resources.description: A marker expressing the author's evaluative attitude toward the proposition rather than shifting its certainty (fortunately, notably, so-called)

resources.label: Modality Category
resources.description: The type of modality the marker expresses

resources.label: Deontic
resources.description: Modality of obligation, permission, and necessity — what the speaker holds should happen (must, should, ought to)

resources.label: Dynamic
resources.description: Modality of ability, willingness, and disposition — the subject's capacity or inclination (can, able to, tends to)

resources.label: Epistemic
resources.description: Modality of knowledge and belief — how certain the speaker is about the truth of the proposition (might, probably, certainly)

resources.label: Evidential
resources.description: Modality of information source — the basis on which the claim rests, whether inference, hearsay, direct perception, or published record (reportedly, according to, research shows)

resources.label: Stance Polarity
resources.description: Whether the author supports, contests, or remains neutral on the proposition

resources.label: Contest
resources.description: The author signals disagreement with or opposition to the proposition (dispute, reject, challenge), whether evidence-grounded, corrective, or adversarial

resources.label: Neutral
resources.description: The author takes no clear evaluative position, reporting or describing without claiming a stake in the outcome (observe, note, report)

resources.label: Support
resources.description: The author signals agreement with or endorsement of the proposition (agree, endorse, advocate), whether on evidential, preferential, or deferential grounds

resources.label: Strength Tier
resources.description: The degree of impact the marker has on perceived certainty

resources.label: Moderate
resources.description: Noticeable impact on perceived certainty — possibly, perhaps, and suggests as hedges; clearly and obviously as boosts

resources.label: Strong
resources.description: Substantial impact on perceived certainty — might, could, and seems as hedges; definitely, must, always, and never as boosts

resources.label: Weak
resources.description: Minimal impact on perceived certainty — approximators such as somewhat and fairly as hedges, likely and probably as boosts

resources.label: Enthusiastic vs Matter-of-Fact
resources.description: The tone dimension running from enthusiastic to matter-of-fact, on which a voice fixes how much energy it carries.

resources.label: Formal vs Casual
resources.description: The tone dimension running from formal to casual, on which a voice fixes its register of address.

resources.label: Funny vs Serious
resources.description: The tone dimension running from funny to serious, on which a voice fixes how much humour it admits.

resources.label: Respectful vs Irreverent
resources.description: The tone dimension running from respectful to irreverent, on which a voice fixes what, if anything, it may treat lightly.

resources.label: Content Structure
resources.description: The organisational pattern of the written content

resources.label: Comparative
resources.description: Side-by-side analysis of options or approaches; suits product comparisons, framework evaluations, and decision guides.

resources.label: Definition Then Benefit
resources.description: Opens with a precise factual definition of the product or concept, then translates each feature into a concrete audience benefit; avoids opening with marketing claims. Suits product descriptions and knowledge-base entries.

resources.label: Hierarchical
resources.description: Top-down organisation moving from general to specific; suits executive summaries, course syllabi, and documentation.

resources.label: Inverted Pyramid
resources.description: Leads with the most important information and lets supporting detail follow in descending significance; the journalistic pattern suited to news articles, executive briefs, and abstracts.

resources.label: Linear
resources.description: Sequential progression from start to finish; suits tutorials, procedures, and narratives.

resources.label: Modular
resources.description: Self-contained sections that can be consumed in any order; suits reference guides, knowledge bases, and FAQs.

resources.label: Problem Solution
resources.description: Establishes a challenge before presenting its resolution; suits case studies, sales content, and thought leadership.

resources.label: Editorial Quality
resources.description: Key quality dimensions evaluated in editorial review

resources.label: Accessibility
resources.description: Usability of the content by readers with disabilities and by assistive technology — navigable structure, meaningful headings, alt text — measured against WCAG 2.1 AA practice.

resources.label: Accuracy
resources.description: Factual and technical correctness: claims, figures, names, and procedures verified against their sources.

resources.label: Benefit Clarity
resources.description: How plainly features are translated into concrete audience benefits, so the reader sees what they gain rather than what the product does.

resources.label: Clarity
resources.description: The degree to which meaning is grasped on first reading: unambiguous wording, concrete referents, and sentences that each carry one proposition.

resources.label: Concision
resources.description: Economy of expression: every word earns its place, with redundancy, filler, and throat-clearing removed without loss of meaning.

resources.label: Consistency
resources.description: Uniform terminology, style, formatting, and voice across a piece and its sibling artifacts, so the same thing is always named the same way.

resources.label: Diagnostic Precision
resources.description: In assessment writing, how sharply an item isolates the specific knowledge or misconception it is meant to test, so a wrong answer reveals why the learner erred.

resources.label: Distractor Plausibility
resources.description: In assessment writing, how credibly the incorrect options reflect real misconceptions, so items discriminate understanding rather than test-taking skill.

resources.label: Feedback Quality
resources.description: In assessment writing, how well formative feedback explains why a response is right or wrong and directs the learner's next step, beyond a bare correct/incorrect verdict.

resources.label: Inclusivity
resources.description: Use of bias-free, culturally aware language that excludes no reader and lets every member of the audience see themselves addressed.

resources.label: Memorability
resources.description: The likelihood that key messages are retained after reading, aided by vivid phrasing, strong structure, and deliberate repetition of core ideas.

resources.label: Specificity
resources.description: Preference for precise, concrete detail — named mechanisms, numbers, examples — over vague buzzwords and generic marketing claims.

resources.label: Tone Alignment
resources.description: Fit between the writing's actual voice and the tone register specified for the piece and its audience.

resources.label: Readability Target
resources.description: The target reading level for the audience

resources.label: Grade 6-8
resources.description: Plain-language band: short sentences and common words for broad general audiences and must-read operational content.

resources.label: Grade 9-12
resources.description: High-school band: standard business prose for general professional audiences, admitting moderate sentence complexity and everyday business vocabulary.

resources.label: Graduate Professional
resources.description: Advanced band: dense, abstraction-heavy prose for expert professional readers, as in white papers and scholarly analysis.

resources.label: Technical Specialist
resources.description: Level defined by domain expertise rather than a grade band: unglossed specialist terminology for practitioners in the field, as in API references and technical specifications.

resources.label: Undergraduate
resources.description: College-level band: sustained argument and discipline-general terminology for educated readers outside the specialism.

resources.label: Tone Register
resources.description: The voice and formality level of the writing

resources.label: Conversational
resources.description: Warm, relatable voice using contractions and direct address; suited to eLearning and video, avoiding passive voice, abstract nouns, and bureaucratic language.

resources.label: Empathetic
resources.description: Supportive, understanding voice that acknowledges challenges; suited to change management and onboarding, never dismissive, trivialising, or jargon-laden.

resources.label: Formal
resources.description: Professional, objective, impersonal voice that avoids contractions, colloquialisms, and first person; suited to executive audiences and regulatory content.

resources.label: Inspirational
resources.description: Motivating, visionary, aspirational voice; suited to keynotes and change communication, avoiding negativity, hedging, and bureaucratic framing.

resources.label: Professional
resources.description: Clear, direct, authoritative but approachable voice — the default register for corporate learning; avoids slang, hedging, superlatives, and marketing framing without specifics.

resources.label: Writing Mode
